# What we are testing??

We want to identify which day 0 PBMC genes are associated with day 7 ASC frequency after influenza vaccination. We're looking at associations rather than prediction, keeping ASC continuous as Arthur suggested. Limma results won't be used for feature selection in elastic net.

We'll include all 29 participants in the main analysis. Two have missing vaccination histories, so we'll replace those values with the median number of prior vaccinations among the other 27 participants. We'll also run sensitivity analyses to see whether different approaches to missing data affect the results.

For limma voom, we'll use the raw gene counts already prepared by the group, followed by TMM normalization and voom

# 1. Packages and existing data

```{r}
# Check that statmod is installed (needed for robust eBayes)
if (!requireNamespace("statmod", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install statmod first: install.packages('statmod')")
}

# Folder for our limma results
out_dir <- here::here("output", "limma_voom")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Load the datasets already prepared by the group
analysis_counts <- readRDS("data/processed/analysis_counts.rds")
meta <- readRDS("data/processed/analysis_metadata.rds")
vaccine_hist <- readRDS("data/vaccine_hist.rds")

# Make sure participants are in the same order
meta <- meta[match(analysis_counts$participant_id, meta$participant_id), ]

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(meta$participant_id),
  identical(analysis_counts$participant_id, meta$participant_id)
)

# Convert RNA-seq data into a matrix for limma
# We need genes in rows and participants in columns
gene_cols <- grep("^ENSG", names(analysis_counts), value = TRUE)

counts <- t(as.matrix(analysis_counts[, gene_cols]))
storage.mode(counts) <- "numeric"

colnames(counts) <- meta$participant_id

# Quick checks
cat("Participants:", ncol(counts), "\n")
cat("Genes before filtering:", nrow(counts), "\n")

```

# 2. Vaccination-history —imp. correction

```{r}

# Started with the original metadata so we can rerun this section
# without adding the same columns multiple times
meta <- readRDS("data/processed/analysis_metadata.rds")

# Keep participants in the same order as the RNA-seq data
meta <- meta[match(analysis_counts$participant_id,
                   meta$participant_id), ]

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(meta$participant_id),
  identical(as.character(meta$participant_id),
            as.character(analysis_counts$participant_id))
)

# Checked that the vaccination-history data has everything we need
stopifnot(
  all(c("subject", "vaccine_year", "received") %in% names(vaccine_hist))
)
# Made sure vaccination years are stored as numbers
vaccine_hist <- vaccine_hist %>%
  mutate(
    vaccine_year = as.integer(as.character(vaccine_year)),
    received = as.character(received)
  )

# Checked for missing years and duplicated yearly records
duplicates <- vaccine_hist %>%
  count(subject, vaccine_year) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(duplicates)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(vaccine_hist$vaccine_year),
  nrow(duplicates) == 0
)

#Count previous vaccinations for each participant
# The 2024 study vaccination should not be counted as previous
vax_summary <- vaccine_hist %>%
  group_by(subject) %>%
  summarise(
    n_prior_corrected = sum(
      vaccine_year < 2024 &
      received %in% c("Yes_Study", "Yes_selfReported")
    ),

    #Check how many 2024 study vaccinations were recorded
    n_study_vax = sum(
      vaccine_year == 2024 & received == "Yes_Study"
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Add the corrected history to our participant data
meta <- meta %>%
  left_join(vax_summary, by = "subject") %>%
  mutate(
    # No vaccination records means unknown, not zero
    vax_missing = is.na(n_prior_corrected),

    # Median imputation for the two missing histories
    n_prior_imputed = if_else(
      vax_missing,
      median(n_prior_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
      as.numeric(n_prior_corrected)
    ),

    # Alternative assumption for sensitivity analysis only
    n_prior_zero = coalesce(n_prior_corrected, 0)
  )

# Check that we still have one row per participant
stopifnot(
  nrow(meta) == nrow(analysis_counts),
  !anyDuplicated(meta$participant_id)
)

# Compared the original count with our corrected count
# We expect a difference of 1 if the old count included 2024
cat("Difference between original and corrected counts:\n")
print(table(
  meta$n_prior_vax - meta$n_prior_corrected,
  useNA = "ifany"
))

# Check missing vaccination histories
cat("\nMissing vaccination histories:\n")
print(table(meta$vax_missing))

# Check the corrected counts
cat("\nCorrected prior vaccination counts:\n")
print(summary(meta$n_prior_corrected))

cat("\nMedian prior vaccinations:\n")
print(median(meta$n_prior_corrected, na.rm = TRUE))

# Check how many study vaccinations were recorded in 2024
cat("\n2024 study vaccination records:\n")
print(table(meta$n_study_vax, useNA = "ifany"))

# Review the final vaccination variables for all participants
vax_audit <- meta %>%
  select(
    participant_id, age, n_prior_vax,
    n_study_vax, n_prior_corrected,
    vax_missing, n_prior_imputed, n_prior_zero
  )

print(as.data.frame(vax_audit))
# Save the audit for the report appendix
write_csv(
  vax_audit,
  file.path(out_dir, "01_vaccination_history_audit.csv")
)

```

# 5.1. Main limma-voom model

```{r}

# 5. Main limma-voom model

# Run the same limma-voom workflow for different models
# This will also be useful for our sensitivity analyses
fit_association <- function(df, formula, asc_term = "log_ASC7",
                            plot_voom = FALSE) {
  
  # Check model variables and match participants to RNA-seq samples
  stopifnot(!anyNA(df[, all.vars(formula), drop = FALSE]))
  
  ids <- match(df$participant_id, colnames(counts_tested))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(ids), !anyDuplicated(df$participant_id))
  
  # Build the regression model
  design <- model.matrix(formula, data = df)
  
  stopifnot(
    qr(design)$rank == ncol(design),
    asc_term %in% colnames(design),
    nrow(design) - ncol(design) >= 8
  )
  
  # TMM normalization, voom weights and gene-wise regression
  dge <- DGEList(counts = counts_tested[, ids, drop = FALSE])
  dge <- normLibSizes(dge, method = "TMM")
  
  v <- voom(dge, design, plot = plot_voom)
  
  fit <- lmFit(v, design)
  fit <- eBayes(fit, robust = TRUE)
  
  # Extract association with ASC and adjust for multiple testing
  results <- topTable(
  fit,
  coef = asc_term,
  number = Inf,
  adjust.method = "BH",
  sort.by = "P"
) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
    rename(beta_ASC = logFC)
  
  
  
  list(
    design = design,
    dge = dge,
    voom = v,
    fit = fit,
    results = results
  )
}

# Main model: Day 7 ASC adjusted for age, sex and previous vaccinations
main_formula <- ~ log_ASC7 + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed

# Save the voom mean-variance diagnostic plot
pdf(file.path(out_dir, "appendix_voom_mean_variance.pdf"),
    width = 8, height = 6)

main <- fit_association(meta, main_formula, plot_voom = TRUE)

dev.off()

# Main results
res <- main$results

cat("Participants:", nrow(main$design), "\n")
cat("Model parameters:", ncol(main$design), "\n")
cat("Residual degrees of freedom:",
    nrow(main$design) - ncol(main$design), "\n")
cat("Genes tested:", nrow(res), "\n")
cat("Nominal p < 0.05:", sum(res$P.Value < 0.05), "\n")
cat("BH FDR < 0.05:", sum(res$adj.P.Val < 0.05), "\n")

# Show the ten strongest associations
print(head(res, 10))

# Save complete results
write_csv(res, file.path(out_dir, "03_limma_main_all_genes.csv"))

# Save significant genes
significant <- res %>% filter(adj.P.Val < 0.05)

write_csv(
  significant,
  file.path(out_dir, "03_limma_main_FDR05.csv")
)

# Prepare GO analysis inputs
write_lines(
  significant$gene_id,
  file.path(out_dir, "GO_foreground_FDR05_Ensembl.txt")
)

write_csv(
  res %>% select(gene_id, beta_ASC, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val),
  file.path(out_dir, "GO_ranked_genes.csv")
)

```

Coefficient interpretation: Here `log_ASC7 = ln(ASC)`. The printed `beta_ASC` estimates how much baseline log₂ gene expression differs per one-unit increase in `ln(ASC)`, holding the covariates constant. For a doubling of ASC, the difference in log₂ expression is `beta_ASC * ln(2)`. We should not use a generic `|logFC| > 1` DEG threshold from the categorical practical.

# 5.2. Sensitivity analyses

```{r}
# Model 1: no vaccination history adjustment
no_vax <- fit_association(
  meta,
  ~ log_ASC7 + age_c + biological_sex
)

# Model 2: Original ASC scale, standardised for interpretation
raw_asc <- fit_association(
  meta,
  ~ ASC7_sd + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed,
  asc_term = "ASC7_sd"
)

# Model 3: Only participants with documented vaccination histories
complete <- fit_association(
  meta %>% filter(!vax_missing),
  ~ log_ASC7 + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_corrected
)

# Model 4: Assume zero previous vaccinations for missing histories
zero_vax <- fit_association(
  meta,
  ~ log_ASC7 + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_zero
)

# Compared results across all models
models <- list(
  Primary = main,
  No_vaccination_adjustment = no_vax,
  Original_ASC_scale = raw_asc,
  Complete_cases = complete,
  Zero_imputation = zero_vax
)

comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(names(models), function(name) {
  x <- models[[name]]

  tibble(
    model = name,
    participants = nrow(x$design),
    nominal_p05 = sum(x$results$P.Value < 0.05),
    FDR_05 = sum(x$results$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
    FDR_10 = sum(x$results$adj.P.Val < 0.10),
    minimum_FDR = min(x$results$adj.P.Val)
  )
}))

print(comparison)

# Saved comparison for the report
write_csv(
  comparison,
  file.path(out_dir, "04_model_sensitivity_comparison.csv")
)

```

```{r}
p_qq <- p_data %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  arrange(p, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n())),
    observed = -log10(pmax(p, .Machine$double.xmin))

  geom_point(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.4, colour = "steelblue") +
```

#6.2. Gene-level diagnostics

```{r}
# Looked at top genes from both models
diagnostic_genes <- unique(c(
  head(raw_asc$results$gene_id, 3),
  head(main$results$gene_id, 3)
))

#Used the same genes for both models
diagnostic_models <- list(
  "Original ASC" = list(
    model = raw_asc,
    formula = ~ ASC7_sd + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed,
    term = "ASC7_sd"
  ),
  "Log ASC" = list(
    model = main,
    formula = ~ log_ASC7 + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed,
    term = "log_ASC7"
  )
)

diagnostics <- list()
associations <- list()

for (model_name in names(diagnostic_models)) {

  spec <- diagnostic_models[[model_name]]

  for (gene in diagnostic_genes) {

    # Voom-normalized gene expression and its precision weights
    df <- meta
    df$expression <- as.numeric(spec$model$voom$E[gene, ])
    w <- as.numeric(
  spec$model$voom$weights[
    match(gene, rownames(spec$model$voom$E)), 
  ]
)

    # Fitted this gene separately to obtain standard regression diagnostics
    gene_fit <- lm(
      update(spec$formula, expression ~ .),
      data = df,
      weights = w
    )

    #Saved residuals, fitted values and influence measures
    diagnostics[[length(diagnostics) + 1]] <- tibble(
      model = model_name,
      gene_id = gene,
      participant_id = df$participant_id,
      fitted = fitted(gene_fit),
      residual = rstandard(gene_fit),
      cooks_d = cooks.distance(gene_fit)
    )

    # Removed the estimated age, sex and vaccination contributions
    #This shows the ASC association after adjustment
    design <- model.matrix(spec$formula, df)
    beta <- coef(gene_fit)

    covariates <- setdiff(
      colnames(design),
      c("(Intercept)", spec$term)
    )

    adjusted_y <- df$expression -
      as.vector(
        design[, covariates, drop = FALSE] %*% beta[covariates]
      )

    associations[[length(associations) + 1]] <- tibble(
      model = model_name,
      gene_id = gene,
      ASC = df[[spec$term]],
      expression = adjusted_y,
      intercept = unname(beta["(Intercept)"]),
      slope = unname(beta[spec$term])
    )
  }
}

diagnostics <- bind_rows(diagnostics)
associations <- bind_rows(associations)

# Plot adjusted gene-expression associations
p_association <- ggplot(
  associations,
  aes(x = ASC, y = expression)
) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(
    aes(intercept = intercept, slope = slope),
    colour = "firebrick"
  ) +
  facet_grid(model ~ gene_id, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "ASC associations adjusted for age, sex and vaccination",
    x = "ASC predictor (model-specific scale)",
    y = "Adjusted baseline log2 expression"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_association)

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "07_adjusted_gene_associations.png"),
  p_association, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300
)

# Weighted standardized residuals versus fitted values
p_resid <- ggplot(diagnostics, aes(fitted, residual)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(model ~ gene_id, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title = "Weighted residuals versus fitted expression",
    x = "Fitted log2 expression",
    y = "Standardized residual"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_resid)

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "07_residuals_vs_fitted.png"),
  p_resid, width = 14, height = 7, dpi = 300
)

# Residual QQ plots
p_resid_qq <- ggplot(diagnostics, aes(sample = residual)) +
  stat_qq(colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  stat_qq_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(model ~ gene_id) +
```

#6.3. Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis

```{r}
# The 78 genes significant in the full original-ASC model
original_sig <- raw_asc$results$gene_id[
  raw_asc$results$adj.P.Val < 0.05
]

# Track the ten strongest genes in more detail
top_genes <- head(raw_asc$results$gene_id, 10)

loo_results <- list()
loo_summary <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(meta))) {

  # Remove one participant
  df_loo <- meta[-i, , drop = FALSE]

  # Refit the original ASC model
  loo_fit <- fit_association(
    df_loo,
    ~ ASC7_sd + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed,
    asc_term = "ASC7_sd"
  )

  r <- loo_fit$results

  # How many associations remain significant?
  loo_summary[[i]] <- tibble(
    removed_participant = meta$participant_id[i],
    genes_FDR05 = sum(r$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
    original_genes_retained = sum(
      original_sig %in% r$gene_id[r$adj.P.Val < 0.05]
    )
  )

  # Record coefficients and significance for the top ten genes
  selected <- r[match(top_genes, r$gene_id), ]

  loo_results[[i]] <- tibble(
    removed_participant = meta$participant_id[i],
    gene_id = selected$gene_id,
    beta = selected$beta_ASC,
    p_value = selected$P.Value,
    FDR = selected$adj.P.Val
  )
}

loo_summary <- bind_rows(loo_summary)
loo_results <- bind_rows(loo_results)

# Compare the strongest genes with their full-data estimates
full_top <- raw_asc$results %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% top_genes) %>%
  select(gene_id, full_beta = beta_ASC)

gene_stability <- loo_results %>%
  left_join(full_top, by = "gene_id") %>%
  group_by(gene_id) %>%
  summarise(
    full_beta = first(full_beta),
    min_beta = min(beta),
    max_beta = max(beta),
    same_direction = sum(sign(beta) == sign(full_beta)),
    FDR05_runs = sum(FDR < 0.05),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("Leave-one-out significance summary:\n")
print(summary(loo_summary$genes_FDR05))

cat("\nNumber of original significant genes retained:\n")
print(summary(loo_summary$original_genes_retained))

cat("\nStability of top ten genes:\n")
print(gene_stability)

# Visualise how many significant genes remain
p_loo <- ggplot(
  loo_summary,
  aes(x = reorder(removed_participant, genes_FDR05),
      y = genes_FDR05)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = length(original_sig),
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "firebrick"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Leave-one-out stability: original ASC model",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = significant genes in the full model",
    x = "Excluded participant",
    y = "Genes with FDR < 0.05"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_loo)

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "07_leave_one_out.png"),
  p_loo, width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300
)

# Save the results
write_csv(
  loo_summary,
  file.path(out_dir, "07_LOO_summary.csv")
)

write_csv(
  gene_stability,
  file.path(out_dir, "07_LOO_gene_stability.csv")
)

write_csv(
  loo_results,
  file.path(out_dir, "07_LOO_gene_details.csv")
)
```

# 7.1. Library sizes and TMM normalization

```{r}
# Made sure the RNA-seq samples and metadata are aligned
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(main$dge$counts),
            as.character(meta$participant_id))
)

# Participants identified as influential in our earlier diagnostics
focus_ids <- c("ID_335", "ID_438", "ID_594",
               "ID_600", "ID_296")

# Extracted sequencing information from the fitted model
sample_qc <- tibble(
  participant_id = colnames(main$dge$counts),
  library_size = main$dge$samples$lib.size,
  TMM_factor = main$dge$samples$norm.factors,
  effective_library_size = library_size * TMM_factor,
  ASC_day7 = meta$ASC_day7,
  age = meta$age
) %>%
  mutate(
    short_id = sub(".*ID_", "ID_", participant_id),
    influential = short_id %in% focus_ids,
    library_millions = library_size / 1e6
  )

# Summarised sequencing characteristics
print(summary(sample_qc %>%
  select(library_size, TMM_factor, effective_library_size)))

# Inspected the four participants in particular
print(sample_qc %>%
  filter(influential) %>%
  select(short_id, library_millions, TMM_factor,
         ASC_day7, age))

# Compared library sizes and TMM factors across participants
qc_long <- sample_qc %>%
  select(short_id, influential, library_millions, TMM_factor) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(library_millions, TMM_factor),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  )

p_qc <- ggplot(qc_long, aes(x = reorder(short_id, value),
                            y = value, colour = influential)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(qc_long, influential),
    aes(label = short_id),
    hjust = -0.15, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
    labels = c("FALSE" = "Other", "TRUE" = "Previously influential")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "RNA-seq library sizes and TMM factors",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Value",
    colour = "Participant"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_qc)

ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "07_library_sizes_TMM.png"),

)

write_csv(
```

#8. Comparing original and log-transformed ASC models \# 8.1. Compared model fit using the same voom weights

```{r}
# Both models used the same 29 participants and 5 parameters
design_log <- main$design
design_raw <- model.matrix(
  ~ ASC7_sd + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed,
  data = meta
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(design_log) == nrow(design_raw),
  ncol(design_log) == ncol(design_raw),
  identical(colnames(main$voom$E), as.character(meta$participant_id))
)

# Kept expression values and weights identical for a fair comparison
fit_log <- lmFit(main$voom, design_log)
fit_raw <- lmFit(main$voom, design_raw)

# Compared weighted residual variation for every gene
rss_log <- fit_log$sigma^2 * fit_log$df.residual
rss_raw <- fit_raw$sigma^2 * fit_raw$df.residual

fit_comparison <- tibble(
  gene_id = rownames(main$voom$E),
  rss_log = rss_log,
  rss_raw = rss_raw,
  log2_rss_ratio = log2(rss_raw / rss_log)
)

# Negative values meant original ASC fitted better
cat("Genes fitted better by original ASC:",
    sum(fit_comparison$log2_rss_ratio < 0), "\n")

cat("Genes fitted better by log ASC:",
    sum(fit_comparison$log2_rss_ratio > 0), "\n")

cat("Percentage favouring original ASC:",
    round(mean(fit_comparison$log2_rss_ratio < 0) * 100, 1),
    "%\n")

print(summary(fit_comparison$log2_rss_ratio))

# Visualised the differences across all tested genes
p_fit <- ggplot(fit_comparison, aes(log2_rss_ratio)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Model fit: original vs log-transformed ASC",
    subtitle = "Negative = original ASC fitted better; positive = log ASC fitted better",
    x = "log2(weighted RSS original / weighted RSS log)",
    y = "Number of genes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p_fit)

ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "08_model_fit_comparison.png"),
       p_fit, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)

write_csv(fit_comparison,
          file.path(out_dir, "08_gene_model_fit.csv"))
```

# 9.2. Compared all tested genes across models

```{r}
# Used the initial log(ASC) model as the reference
reference <- main$results

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(reference$gene_id),
  !anyNA(reference$t)
)

consistency <- bind_rows(lapply(names(models)[-1], function(name) {

  r <- models[[name]]$results

  # Matched the same genes in both models
  idx <- match(reference$gene_id, r$gene_id)

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(idx),
    !anyDuplicated(r$gene_id),
    nrow(r) == nrow(reference)
  )

  r <- r[idx, ]

  tibble(
    model = name,

    # Agreement in signed association statistics
    signed_t_correlation = cor(
      reference$t, r$t, method = "spearman"
    ),

    # Agreement in overall association strength
    strength_correlation = cor(
      abs(reference$t), abs(r$t), method = "spearman"
    ),

    # Percentage of genes with the same association direction
    same_direction_pct = 100 * mean(
      sign(reference$t) == sign(r$t)
    )
  )
}))

print(consistency)

write_csv(
  consistency,
  file.path(out_dir, "09_genome_wide_consistency.csv")
)
```

#10. Sensitivity analysis - does gene filtering change our results? \# 10.1. Repeated the primary model with design-based gene filtering

```{r}
# Started from the original raw counts
dge_design <- DGEList(counts = counts)

# Used the same regression design to set the expression filter
keep_design <- filterByExpr(dge_design, design = main$design)
dge_design <- dge_design[keep_design, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]

# Recalculated library normalization for the new gene set
dge_design <- normLibSizes(dge_design, method = "TMM")

# Checked that samples were in the same order as our metadata
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(dge_design$counts),
            as.character(meta$participant_id)),
  nrow(main$design) == ncol(dge_design$counts),
  qr(main$design)$rank == ncol(main$design)
)

# Repeated voom and limma with the new gene set
v_design <- voom(dge_design, main$design, plot = FALSE)

fit_design <- lmFit(v_design, main$design)
fit_design <- eBayes(fit_design, robust = TRUE)

# Extracted the ASC association for all retained genes
res_design <- topTable(
  fit_design,
  coef = "log_ASC7",
  number = Inf,
  adjust.method = "BH",
  sort.by = "P"
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  rename(beta_ASC = logFC)

cat("Genes tested:", nrow(res_design), "\n")
cat("Nominal p < 0.05:", sum(res_design$P.Value < 0.05), "\n")
cat("BH FDR < 0.05:", sum(res_design$adj.P.Val < 0.05), "\n")
cat("Minimum FDR:", min(res_design$adj.P.Val), "\n")

print(head(res_design, 10))

write_csv(
  res_design,
  file.path(out_dir, "10_design_filter_all_genes.csv")
)
```

#11. Exploratory analysis - does day 0 ASC explain part of the day 7 associations? a# 11.1. Loaded and checked day 0 and day 7 ASC measurements

```{r}

# 11.1. Loaded and checked the original ASC measurements

flow <- read_csv(
  here::here("data", "publicData_ex_vivo_flow.csv"),
  col_types = cols(
    timepoint = col_character(),
    .default = col_guess()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Kept Day 0 and Day 7 ASC measurements from our cohort
asc_flow <- flow %>%
  filter(
    study_accession == "2024_UGA",
    name == "Antibody-secreting_cells_(ASC)",
    timepoint %in% c("0", "7")
  )

# Checked sample counts, units and cell population
flow_check <- asc_flow %>%
  group_by(timepoint, unit, parent_population) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(participant_id), .groups = "drop")

print(flow_check)

# Confirmed that the records were unique and comparable
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(asc_flow[c("participant_id", "timepoint")]),
  n_distinct(asc_flow$unit) == 1,
  n_distinct(asc_flow$parent_population) == 1,
  all(is.finite(asc_flow$value))
)

# Extracted Day 0 ASC
day0 <- asc_flow %>%
  filter(timepoint == "0") %>%
  select(participant_id, ASC_day0 = value)

# Checked Day 7 against the values already used in limma
day7 <- asc_flow %>%
  filter(timepoint == "7") %>%
  select(participant_id, ASC_day7_flow = value)

check7 <- meta %>%
  left_join(day7, by = "participant_id")

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(check7$ASC_day7_flow),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    check7$ASC_day7,
    check7$ASC_day7_flow,
    tolerance = 1e-6
  ))
)

cat("Day 7 ASC values matched our existing data.\n")
```

```{r}
stopifnot(

)

#Checked whether baseline ASC was related to Day 7 ASC

# Used logarithmic axes to make the skewed values easier to see
```

#11.3. Checked whether baseline ASC adjustment changed the results

```{r}
# Standardised Day 0 ASC to avoid very small coefficients
paired <- paired %>%
  mutate(ASC0_sd = as.numeric(scale(ASC_day0)))

stopifnot(
  nrow(paired) >= 15,
  all(is.finite(paired$ASC0_sd)),
  !anyNA(paired$n_prior_imputed)
)

# Model without baseline ASC adjustment
paired_basic <- fit_association(
  paired,
  ~ log_ASC7 + age_c + biological_sex + n_prior_imputed
)

# Same model, now accounting for baseline ASC
paired_adjusted <- fit_association(
  paired,
  ~ log_ASC7 + ASC0_sd + age_c +
    biological_sex + n_prior_imputed
)

# Matched gene results from both models
paired_compare <- paired_basic$results %>%
  select(
    gene_id,
    beta_without = beta_ASC,
    t_without = t,
    p_without = P.Value
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    paired_adjusted$results %>%
      select(
        gene_id,
        beta_with = beta_ASC,
        t_with = t,
        p_with = P.Value
      ),
    by = "gene_id"
  )

# Summarised the change in associations
paired_summary <- tibble(
  participants = nrow(paired),
  genes_tested = nrow(paired_compare),
  t_correlation = cor(
    paired_compare$t_without,
    paired_compare$t_with,
    method = "spearman"
  ),
  same_direction_pct = 100 * mean(
    sign(paired_compare$beta_without) ==
    sign(paired_compare$beta_with)
  ),
  FDR05_without = sum(
    paired_basic$results$adj.P.Val < 0.05
  ),
  FDR05_with = sum(
    paired_adjusted$results$adj.P.Val < 0.05
  )
)

print(as.data.frame(paired_summary))

write_csv(
  paired_summary,
  file.path(out_dir, "11_day0_adjustment_summary.csv")
)

write_csv(
  paired_compare,
  file.path(out_dir, "11_day0_gene_comparison.csv")
)

write_csv(
  paired_adjusted$results,
  file.path(out_dir, "11_day0_adjusted_results.csv")
)
```

#12.5.1. Built GO Biological Process gene sets

```{r}
# Removed any Ensembl version suffixes
gene_ids <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", rownames(main$voom$E))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(gene_ids))

# Retrieved all inherited GO Biological Process annotations
go_map <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys = gene_ids,
  columns = c("GOALL", "ONTOLOGYALL"),
  keytype = "ENSEMBL"
) %>%
  filter(
    ONTOLOGYALL == "BP",
    !is.na(GOALL)
  ) %>%
  distinct(ENSEMBL, GOALL)

# Converted gene IDs into row positions for CAMERA
go_sets <- split(
  match(go_map$ENSEMBL, gene_ids),
  go_map$GOALL
)

go_sets <- lapply(go_sets, function(x) unique(na.omit(x)))

# Kept informative pathway sizes
go_sets <- go_sets[
  lengths(go_sets) >= 15 &
  lengths(go_sets) <= 500
]

stopifnot(length(go_sets) > 0)

# Retrieved readable GO names
go_names <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  GO.db::GO.db,
  keys = names(go_sets),
  columns = "TERM",
  keytype = "GOID"
) %>%
  distinct(GOID, .keep_all = TRUE)

go_universe <- tibble(
  GO_ID = names(go_sets),
  genes_in_set = lengths(go_sets)
) %>%
  left_join(go_names, by = c("GO_ID" = "GOID"))

cat("Genes with BP annotations:",
    n_distinct(go_map$ENSEMBL), "\n")

cat("GO terms tested:", length(go_sets), "\n")

write_csv(
  go_universe,
  file.path(go_dir, "CAMERA_GO_terms_tested.csv")
)

```

# 12.5.2. Tested GO sets under both ASC models

```{r}
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(main$voom$E),
            rownames(raw_asc$voom$E))
)

# Used the same GO sets for both models
camera_log <- limma::camera(
  main$voom,
  index = go_sets,
  design = main$design,
  contrast = which(colnames(main$design) == "log_ASC7"),
  inter.gene.cor = 0.01
)

camera_raw <- limma::camera(
  raw_asc$voom,
  index = go_sets,
  design = raw_asc$design,
  contrast = which(colnames(raw_asc$design) == "ASC7_sd"),
  inter.gene.cor = 0.01
)

# Added GO IDs and readable names
format_camera <- function(results) {
  results %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("GO_ID") %>%
    left_join(go_universe, by = "GO_ID") %>%
    arrange(PValue)
}

camera_log <- format_camera(camera_log)
camera_raw <- format_camera(camera_raw)

# Summarised the results
camera_summary <- tibble(
  model = c("Log ASC", "Original ASC"),
  terms_tested = c(nrow(camera_log), nrow(camera_raw)),
  FDR05 = c(
    sum(camera_log$FDR < 0.05),
    sum(camera_raw$FDR < 0.05)
  ),
  minimum_FDR = c(
    min(camera_log$FDR),
    min(camera_raw$FDR)
  )
)

print(camera_summary)

cat("\nStrongest GO terms under log ASC:\n")
print(head(camera_log, 10))

cat("\nStrongest GO terms under original ASC:\n")
print(head(camera_raw, 10))

write_csv(
  camera_log,
  file.path(go_dir, "CAMERA_log_ASC.csv")
)

write_csv(
  camera_raw,
  file.path(go_dir, "CAMERA_original_ASC.csv")
)

write_csv(
  camera_summary,
  file.path(go_dir, "CAMERA_summary.csv")
)
```

# 12.5.5. Checked sensitivity to the inter-gene correlation assumption

```{r}
# Re-ran the primary model with correlation estimated for each gene set
camera_estimated <- limma::camera(
  main$voom,
  index = go_sets,
```

# 12.7. Imported the online GO enrichment results

```{r}
# Read the DAVID Functional Annotation Chart
david <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(go_dir, "DAVID_chart.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  transmute(
    GO_ID = stringr::str_extract(`Full Term`, "GO:[0-9]+"),
    TERM = Term,
    DAVID_FDR = Benjamini,
    DAVID_fold = `Fold Enrichment`
  )

# Imported PANTHER results and handled very small fold enrichment values

panther <- readr::read_tsv(
  file.path(go_dir, "PANTHER_results.txt"),
  skip = 11,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  transmute(
    GO_ID = stringr::str_extract(.data[[names(.)[1]]], "GO:[0-9]+"),
    PANTHER_FDR = as.numeric(.data[[names(.)[8]]]),
    PANTHER_fold = as.numeric(
      ifelse(
        grepl("<", .data[[names(.)[6]]]),
        NA,
        .data[[names(.)[6]]]
      )
    )
  )

# GOrilla exports are tab-separated files despite the .xls extension
read_gorilla <- function(filename, label) {
  readr::read_tsv(
    file.path(go_dir, filename),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    transmute(
      GO_ID = `GO Term`,
      FDR = `FDR q-value`
    ) %>%
    rename(!!paste0("GOrilla_", label, "_FDR") := FDR)
}

gorilla_pos <- read_gorilla("GOrilla_positive.xls", "positive")
gorilla_neg <- read_gorilla("GOrilla_negative.xls", "negative")

# Used the CAMERA results already calculated before
camera_final <- camera_log %>%
  select(
    GO_ID,
    CAMERA_fixed_FDR = FDR
  ) %>%
  left_join(

      select(GO_ID, CAMERA_estimated_FDR = FDR),
    by = "GO_ID"
  )

# Checked that GO IDs were unique within each result table

  !anyDuplicated(panther$GO_ID),
  !anyDuplicated(gorilla_pos$GO_ID),
  !anyDuplicated(gorilla_neg$GO_ID),
  !anyDuplicated(camera_final$GO_ID)
)

cat("DAVID terms:", nrow(david), "\n")
cat("PANTHER terms:", nrow(panther), "\n")
cat("GOrilla positive terms:", nrow(gorilla_pos), "\n")
cat("GOrilla negative terms:", nrow(gorilla_neg), "\n")
cat("CAMERA terms:", nrow(camera_final), "\n")
```

# 12.8. Matched biological processes across enrichment methods

```{r}

# Retrieved readable names for GO identifiers across the tools
all_go_ids <- unique(na.omit(c(
  david$GO_ID,
  panther$GO_ID,
  gorilla_pos$GO_ID,
  gorilla_neg$GO_ID,
  camera_final$GO_ID
)))

go_labels <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  GO.db::GO.db,
  keys = all_go_ids,
  columns = "TERM",
  keytype = "GOID"
) %>%
  distinct(GOID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  rename(GO_ID = GOID, TERM_annotation = TERM)

# Combined results, excluding records without a GO identifier
go_final <- david %>%
  full_join(
    panther %>% filter(!is.na(GO_ID)),
    by = "GO_ID"
  ) %>%
  full_join(gorilla_pos, by = "GO_ID") %>%
  full_join(gorilla_neg, by = "GO_ID") %>%
  full_join(camera_final, by = "GO_ID") %>%
  left_join(go_labels, by = "GO_ID") %>%
  mutate(
    TERM = coalesce(TERM, TERM_annotation),
    DAVID_sig = !is.na(DAVID_FDR) & DAVID_FDR < 0.05,
    PANTHER_sig = !is.na(PANTHER_FDR) & PANTHER_FDR < 0.05,
    GOrilla_positive_sig = !is.na(GOrilla_positive_FDR) &
      GOrilla_positive_FDR < 0.05,
    GOrilla_negative_sig = !is.na(GOrilla_negative_FDR) &
      GOrilla_negative_FDR < 0.05,
    CAMERA_fixed_sig = !is.na(CAMERA_fixed_FDR) &
      CAMERA_fixed_FDR < 0.05,
    CAMERA_estimated_sig = !is.na(CAMERA_estimated_FDR) &
      CAMERA_estimated_FDR < 0.05
  ) %>%
  select(-TERM_annotation)

cat("GO terms without readable names:",
    sum(is.na(go_final$TERM)), "\n")

# Summarised the significant GO terms
go_final_summary <- tibble(
  Method = c(
    "DAVID",
    "PANTHER",
    "GOrilla positive",
    "GOrilla negative",
    "CAMERA fixed correlation",
    "CAMERA estimated correlation"
  ),
  Significant_terms = c(
    sum(go_final$DAVID_sig),
    sum(go_final$PANTHER_sig),
    sum(go_final$GOrilla_positive_sig),
    sum(go_final$GOrilla_negative_sig),
    sum(go_final$CAMERA_fixed_sig),
    sum(go_final$CAMERA_estimated_sig)
  )
)

print(go_final_summary)

# Checked DAVID/PANTHER agreement
cat(
  "GO terms significant in both DAVID and PANTHER:",
  sum(go_final$DAVID_sig & go_final$PANTHER_sig),
  "\n"
)

# Checked which DAVID/PANTHER terms also appeared in negative GOrilla
cat(
  "DAVID/PANTHER significant terms also significant in negative GOrilla:",
  sum(
    go_final$DAVID_sig &
    go_final$PANTHER_sig &
    go_final$GOrilla_negative_sig
  ),
  "\n"
)

write_csv(
  go_final,
  file.path(go_dir, "GO_final_all_methods.csv")
)

write_csv(
  go_final_summary,
  file.path(go_dir, "GO_final_summary.csv")
)
```

# 12.10. Compared DAVID and PANTHER enrichment visually

```{r}
# Selected GO terms significant in both DAVID and PANTHER
plot_terms <- go_final %>%
  filter(DAVID_sig, PANTHER_sig) %>%
  arrange(DAVID_FDR) %>%
  pull(GO_ID)

plot_data <- go_final %>%
  filter(GO_ID %in% plot_terms) %>%
  select(GO_ID, TERM, DAVID_FDR, PANTHER_FDR) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(DAVID_FDR, PANTHER_FDR),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "FDR"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(FDR)) %>%
  mutate(
    Method = recode(
      Method,
      DAVID_FDR = "DAVID",
      PANTHER_FDR = "PANTHER"
    ),
    score = -log10(pmax(FDR, .Machine$double.xmin)),
    TERM = factor(
      TERM,
      levels = rev(
        go_final$TERM[match(plot_terms, go_final$GO_ID)]
      )
    )
  )

p_go_final <- ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = score, y = TERM, colour = Method)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = -log10(0.05),
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "GO Biological Process enrichment",
    subtitle = "GO terms significant in both DAVID and PANTHER",
    x = expression(-log[10]("FDR-adjusted p-value")),
    y = NULL,
    colour = "Method",
    caption = "Dashed line: FDR = 0.05. Exploratory nominal-p gene list."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

print(p_go_final)

ggsave(
  file.path(go_dir, "GO_DAVID_PANTHER_comparison.png"),
  p_go_final,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```
